1_parties_and_buyer_credit.value: Seller is Havrebakke Vind ApS. Buyer is Jutland Board & Packaging A/S, which is unrated. The Buyer's payment obligations are guaranteed by its parent, Jutland Industri Holding A/S, through a parent company guarantee in Annex 4. The Buyer also posts a letter of credit (see credit support).
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.quote: Seller: Havrebakke Vind ApS. Buyer: Jutland Board & Packaging A/S, unrated. Payment obligations guaranteed by Jutland Industri Holding A/S.
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.clause: Part I; Part II 9.2; Annex 4 (as cited in the due diligence summary, section 2)
1_parties_and_buyer_credit.note: This is a lawyers' summary, not the PPA. No rating trigger is mentioned, and the Buyer is unrated. The summary says the parent guarantee is the credit the committee relies on.

2_facility.value: Onshore wind farm of eight turbines with 48.0 MW capacity at Havrebakke, Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, Denmark, in bidding zone DK1.
2_facility.quote: Eight onshore turbines, 48.0 MW, Havrebakke, Ringkøbing-Skjern Municipality, DK1.
2_facility.note: The summary gives one capacity figure and does not say whether it is AC or DC.

3_supply_period.value: The Supply Period is ten years and starts on the Commercial Operation Date. The Target COD is 1 October 2027.
3_supply_period.quote: The Supply Period runs ten (10) years from the Commercial Operation Date.

4_cod_and_delay.value: Target COD is 1 October 2027 and the Longstop Date is 31 March 2028. Delay damages are EUR 9,600 per day after the Target COD, capped at EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.quote: Target COD 1 October 2027. Longstop Date 31 March 2028. Delay damages EUR 9,600 per day after the Target COD, capped at EUR 1,750,000.
4_cod_and_delay.note: Failure to reach COD by the Longstop Date is an Event of Default (Part II 12–13).

5_price_and_indexation.value: The Contract Price is EUR 54.50 per MWh, stated in the Election Sheet (Annex 2). Thirty per cent of the price is adjusted annually from 1 January 2029 by the Danish consumer price index.
5_price_and_indexation.quote: EUR 54.50 per MWh per the Election Sheet. Thirty per cent of the price is adjusted annually from 1 January 2029 by the Danish consumer price index.
5_price_and_indexation.note: The figure is taken from the lawyers' summary of the Election Sheet. The Election Sheet itself is not attached.

6_volume_and_performance.value: Pay-as-produced: 100 % of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production is 158,000 MWh (P50). Minimum Annual Production is 118,500 MWh, with a shortfall payment as the remedy.
6_volume_and_performance.quote: 100 % of Metered Output. Expected Annual Production 158,000 MWh (P50). Minimum Annual Production 118,500 MWh with a shortfall payment.
6_volume_and_performance.note: The summary does not say how the shortfall payment is calculated. The summary calls the agreement a pay-as-produced physical PPA.

7_product_and_certificates.value: The Seller sells electricity and all Guarantees of Origin, which are transferred at no additional cost. There is no capacity product.
7_product_and_certificates.quote: Electricity and all Guarantees of Origin, transferred at no additional cost. No capacity product.
7_product_and_certificates.note: No GO volume is stated. The summary says all GOs are transferred.

8_curtailment.value: The Buyer may instruct reductions for up to 150 hours per Contract Year. These are paid as Deemed Delivered Electricity at the Contract Price. Reductions instructed by the transmission system operator are not compensated by the Buyer. The summary notes the Seller has no equivalent curtailment right.
8_curtailment.quote: Buyer may instruct reductions for up to 150 hours per Contract Year, paid as Deemed Delivered Electricity at the Contract Price. Reductions instructed by the transmission system operator are not compensated by the Buyer.
8_curtailment.note: The cap is stated in hours only, with no MWh cap. Treatment of negative prices is not addressed in the summary. It does not say whether TSO-curtailed energy counts as deemed delivered, only that the Buyer does not compensate it.

9_delivery_point_and_balancing.value: Physical delivery at the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation. The Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears imbalance costs from COD.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.quote: Physical delivery at the metering point on the 60 kV side of the Havrebakke substation. Buyer appoints the balance responsible party and bears imbalance costs from COD.
9_delivery_point_and_balancing.note: Settlement is physical, so no financial reference price applies.

10_credit_support.value: Seller: bank guarantee of EUR 2,000,000 from Financial Close until twelve months after COD. Buyer: parent company guarantee plus a letter of credit equal to nine months of expected payments.
10_credit_support.quote: Seller: bank guarantee EUR 2,000,000 from Financial Close until twelve months after COD. Buyer: parent company guarantee plus a letter of credit equal to nine months of expected payments.
10_credit_support.note: The Buyer's letter of credit is sized as nine months of expected payments, with no EUR amount given. The duration of the Buyer's parent guarantee and letter of credit is not stated in the summary.

11_default_and_termination.value: Events of Default include non-payment within ten Business Days of notice, insolvency, and failure to reach COD by the Longstop Date. The Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remaining Supply Period.
11_default_and_termination.quote: Non-payment within ten Business Days of notice, insolvency and failure to reach COD by the Longstop Date are Events of Default. Termination Amount is the present value of the difference between the Contract Price and the Reference Forward Price over the remaining Supply Period.
11_default_and_termination.note: The formula is described in the summary. The summary does not name the forward curve source for the Reference Forward Price. It says only that the PPA names a published DK1 forward curve. The discount rate and which party pays are not stated. The list of Events of Default is not shown as complete.

12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.value: A cost impact from Change in Law above EUR 250,000 in a Contract Year triggers good-faith renegotiation. If there is no agreement within 90 days, the affected Party may terminate without a Termination Amount. Force majeure lasting more than 180 consecutive days gives either Party a termination right.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.quote: A cost impact above EUR 250,000 in a Contract Year triggers good-faith renegotiation; absent agreement within 90 days the affected Party may terminate without a Termination Amount.
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.clause: Part II 11 (change in law); Part II 10 (force majeure)
12_change_in_law_and_force_majeure.note: The summary does not say which party bears change-in-law cost below the EUR 250,000 threshold. It calls the termination right mutual and says lenders are expected to ask for it to be tightened.
